implementation_notes: Modified only the supplied module and this report. No commits, installation or external actions were performed; shell commands were rtk-prefixed and all Go commands used the required local toolchain/workspace/cache settings.

Export retains func(io.Reader, io.WriteCloser) (int, error) and forwards to ExportLimit with zero. ExportLimit takes an int limit, rejects negatives before input/output I/O, and closes its owned writer exactly once while leaving the borrowed reader open.
Finalization returns a single operation/Close error unchanged and errors.Join only when both fail, preserving errors.Is/As inspection for both independent causes.

The loop checks a positive limit before scanning another record and reports success once the limit is reached, including when buffered input carried a later read error. Empty and final unterminated records count and are newline-terminated in output.
Accepted counts exclude failed or short writes. A nil-error short write produces io.ErrShortWrite and stops further reads/writes; partial bytes already written remain visible.

The CLI accepts INPUT OUTPUT [LIMIT] without a flag parser, parses a non-negative decimal int before opening files, preserves '-' path names, and routes success/failure/invalid usage through exit statuses 0/1/2 with the promised streams.

Tests cover independent read/write/Close failures and their combinations, direct error identity and typed Close causes, exactly-once writer closing and borrowed reader lifetime, zero/positive/negative limits, exact and above-count bounds, empty and unterminated records, scanning order, read-error-with-data boundaries, partial-write prefixes and short writes.

Actual built-CLI tests verify default/zero/positive limits, positional '-' paths, invalid/missing/extra/negative/overflow arguments without truncation, input/open failures, stdout/stderr and status, and accepted prefix retention on a scanner failure. Temporary files and bounded subprocess contexts are independently owned by each test.
README and Godoc describe API usage, ownership, joined errors, positional CLI usage, exit statuses, short writes, Scanner limitations and partial output, without task-history documentation.
